title: When Do LLMs Generate Realistic Social Networks? A Multi-Dimensional Study of Culture, Language, Scale, and Method

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring inbreeding homophily (same-group tie formation ratio) based on political affiliation in LLM-generated directed social networks across different prompt architectures, cultural framings, and languages.
Measuring inbreeding homophily based on religion in generated networks, specifically evaluating how prompt language (e.g., Hindi, English) shifts the rate of same-religion tie formation.
Measuring inbreeding homophily for age groups, specifically observing how different prompt architectures (like global generation) elevate age as a dominant dimension for tie formation.
Measuring the same-group ratio (inbreeding homophily) for gender in LLM-generated social networks.
Measuring the same-group ratio (inbreeding homophily) for race and ethnicity in LLM-generated social networks.

Evaluating structural changes (e.g., network cohesiveness, largest connected component) and homophily shifts in generated networks when the prompt explicitly varies the cultural context (US, India, Japan, Brazil).

Varying prompt language (English, Spanish, Hindi, Japanese) while holding the persona roster and cultural framing constant to observe shifts in the demographic biases of the resulting simulated social networks.
